newsitem.title: SPAIN: MOTOR CYCLING-CRIVILLE LEADS FROM START TO FINISH.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR CYCLING-CRIVILLE LEADS FROM START TO FINISH.

text.p: Alex Criville made amends for crashing in sight of the finish line last year to beat arch-rival Michael Doohan in the Spanish 500 cc motorcycle Grand Prix on Sunday.
Criville led from start to finish. He never looked in danger from the three-times world champion who struggled to take second place from another Honda man, Tadayuki Okada.
"It's a dream for me, I couldn't ask for more, in front of the fans and the King," said Criville, who had to fight back tears while receiving the winners' trophy from King Juan Carlos.
In last year's race Criville had crashed near the finish after slowing to avoid fans who were already celebrating his victory.
The win also enabled Criville to close to within five points of world championship leader Doohan.
Criville surged to the front at the first bend after starting the race third on the grid.

The only opposition to Criville came from another local favourite Carlos Checa but he crashed on the fifth lap while second, and shortly afterwards the Spanish fans saw Jerez specialist Alberto Puig go the same way.
But a home victory was never in doubt as Criville opened a lead of over six seconds at the halfway stage, before easing up in the final section.
Behind him it was in the last few laps only that Doohan had looked likely to catch pole position Okada who had been on pole.
"There are really no excuses. Alex rode a really good race. I was really lucky to finish where I did," said Doohan.
Doohan replied with a joke when he was asked if he had been waiting for the last lap to attack Okada.
"I was waiting for the last lap the whole way round," he said.
The highlight of the other category races were spectacular comebacks by two Italian riders.
Teenager Valentino Rossi tore his way through the field to take his second Grand Prix of the season in an exciting 125 cc race.

Rossi was left back in 13th place after a poor start. But a string of best laps took him up to the leaders and he snatched victory on the last lap after taking advantage of a mistake by Japan's Noboru Ueda.
Ueda admitted afterwards that he had slipped a gear after opening up the throttle too much.
Rossi's ride was rivalled onlyby an extraordinary performance from compatriot Max Biaggi, the reigning 250 cc world champion.
Biaggi clawed his way back to take third place after coming off the track early in the race, an error that had left him back in 24th position.
But Biaggi's surge came too late to dent the lead of German Ralf Waldmann. He dominated the race after seeing rivals Loris Capirossi and Tohru Ukawa collide on the first curve.
